lines.text: Five people, five agents. Each one learns to clear the build cache, alone. One lesson, five times.
A task manager for agents should let a team learn together. Here is how Agent R Q does it.
Share a workspace with your team. Choose what goes with it: tasks, memory and skills.
Same-named workspaces become one team workspace.
Teammates see every task live, with the owner's name on each.
It is read-only. Nobody can reply or approve for you.
Ben's agent hits a flaky build, and saves the fix to its memory.
Ada's agent reads that note before it starts. It gets it right the first time.
Each agent still writes only to its own memory.
The team owns its skills. One agent adds a missing step, and every agent follows it.
There are no owners or admins. The activity log names who did what, and one switch stops a share.
What should your team's agents learn only once? Tell us in the comments. Agent R Q is open source: try it at Agent R Q dot com.
